record.paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
record.context_brief: Cuts and unbounded paths through trees
record.original_question: Let D be a regular ultrafilter on I with |I| = λ. Let κ1 and κ2 be infinite regular cardinals with λ ≤ κ1 + κ2 < 2^λ, and suppose the ultrapower (ω,<)^I/D has a (κ1,κ2)-cut. If κ = κ1 + κ2, must there be some tree T, in the sense of a partially ordered set whose predecessors of any node are well ordered, such that the ultrapower T^λ/D contains a strictly increasing κ-indexed sequence with no upper bound?

evidence.quote: By a tree we will mean a partially ordered set in which the set of predecessors of any given node is well ordered.
Problem 1.13 ... Is it necessarily the case that for some tree T ... there is a strictly increasing κ-indexed sequence ...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A tree is a partially ordered set $(T,\le_T)$ in which, for every $t\in T$, the set $\{s\in T : s<_T t\}$ of predecessors of $t$ is well-ordered by $<_T$. For an ultrafilter $D$ on a set $I$ and a structure $M$, write $M^I/D$ for the ultrapower of $M$ modulo $D$; if $M$ is a partial order, $M^I/D$ inherits a partial order. An ultrafilter $D$ on $I$ is regular if there is a family $\{X_i : i\in I\}\subseteq D$ such that every infinite subfamily has empty intersection. Given regular infinite cardinals $\kappa_1,\kappa_2$, a $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$-cut in a linear order $(L,<)$ is a pair of sequences $(a_\alpha)_{\alpha<\kappa_1}$, $(b_\beta)_{\beta<\kappa_2}$ in $L$ such that $a_\alpha < a_{\alpha'} < b_{\beta'} < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha<\alpha'<\kappa_1$, $\beta<\beta'<\kappa_2$, and there is no $c\in L$ with $a_\alpha < c < b_\beta$ for all $\alpha,\beta$.

Problem. Let $I$ be a set with $|I|=\lambda$ and let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $I$. Let $\kappa_1,\kappa_2$ be infinite regular cardinals with $\lambda \le \kappa_1+\kappa_2 < 2^\lambda$, and suppose that the ultrapower $(\omega,<)^I/D$ has a $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$-cut. Set $\kappa = \kappa_1+\kappa_2$. Must there exist a tree $T$ (in the sense above) such that the ultrapower $T^I/D$, with its induced partial order, contains a strictly increasing $\kappa$-indexed sequence having no upper bound in $T^I/D$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a definitive resolution of this specific question relating $(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$-cuts in regular ultrapowers of $(\omega,<)$ to the existence of unbounded $\kappa$-indexed strictly increasing sequences in some tree ultrapower. Related work by Malliaris and Shelah on cofinality spectrum problems and treetops is closely connected, and they show that $\lambda^+$-treetops are equivalent to goodness, but this does not directly settle the question as stated. Current status appears to be unknown/open from available sources.
